lead.headline: Teaching in Swedish prisons is a practice of its own, study finds
lead.standfirst: Interviews with 14 adult educators in Swedish prisons show a pedagogy built on trust, responsibility and empowerment.
body: It is negotiated between care and control, autonomy and coercion, trust and vigilance, the authors write.
lead.more: Adult education in Swedish prisons (International Journal of Lifelong Education).

five.headline: Teachers and trainers are key agents of change, says the ETF
five.standfirst: As AI and the green transition reshape labour markets, the ETF argues for investing in the educators who support young people and adults throughout their learning.
five.more: ETF: why investing in teachers and trainers matters.

five.headline: Cedefop describes Ireland’s further education and training system
five.standfirst: A new short description covers VET for learners aged 16+ and adults, delivered mainly through 16 education and training boards.
body: It highlights the dual apprenticeship model, tertiary degrees linking further and higher education, and microqualifications under the Skills to Advance initiative.
five.more: VET in Ireland: Cedefop short description and Spotlight.

five.headline: Agency board changes for Cedefop, Eurofound and EU-OSHA
five.standfirst: The Council replaced a member of Cedefop’s Management Board for Bulgaria (decision of 24 September).
body: It also replaced a member and an alternate for Denmark at Eurofound (9 October) and members for Estonia and Cyprus at EU-OSHA (1 October).
five.more: Board changes at Cedefop, Eurofound and EU-OSHA (Official Journal).

five.headline: New apprenticeship policies in Cedefop’s 2025 timeline update
five.standfirst: First reported in the 2025 update by Cedefop and ReferNet, as summarised on Apprentix.
body: They include Denmark’s substantial reinforcement of VET and mandatory work experience, Greece’s 2025–2027 strategic plan for VET, lifelong learning and youth, Slovakia’s tertiary VET reinforcement and Slovenia’s programme document for development planning until 2033.
five.more: New apprenticeship policies in Cedefop’s 2025 timeline update.

five.headline: EU leaders and social partners meet at the Tripartite Social Summit
five.standfirst: The twice-yearly summit brought EU leaders and social partners together in Brussels on 14 October.
five.more: Tripartite Social Summit, 14 October: EU leaders and social partners.

more.headline: Vienna debates how young people find a way into apprenticeships
more.standfirst: At the Tag der Wiener Jugend, experts discussed the difficult search for apprenticeships and the falling number of training companies, Der Standard reports.
body: The head of Austria’s public employment service, AMS, told the event he is interested in applicants who have changed course.
more.more: Vienna: experts on young people’s hard search for apprenticeships (Der Standard).

lives.headline: What world gold cost a young cabinetmaker
lives.standfirst: Tobias Kelz won WorldSkills gold in Shanghai by a single point, finishing his piece in the last second.
body: He had 22 hours to build a piece of furniture he first saw on day one, with solid wood, panels, veneer and doors to hang, and made two careless mistakes along the way; his trainer, whom he could only consult in breaks, found a way to recover. In the evenings they negotiated every minute of the next day’s time.

The road began after his journeyman’s exam, more than two years earlier: the chamber, Bavarian and national competitions, then a year of training with the other national winners before the trainers picked two cabinetmakers for Shanghai. In the last six months there was no real free time: a week a month at the wood technical school in Bad Wildungen, work by day, the workshop after hours. Some days, he says, he asked himself why he was doing it; his employer accepted many absences.
What he takes away: new techniques, more speed, and more calm. He would do it again, he says, but not a second time.
